D019-D005_h001.question:
It’s been a few weeks since I got laid off, and ever since then my sleep’s been a mess. I fall asleep okay, but I keep jolting awake two, three times a night and then just lie there, staring at the ceiling, my mind going over everything that happened at work. Sometimes it feels like I barely sleep at all, even though my wife says I was out for a few hours.

Certain things set me off in a way that feels…bigger than it should be. Getting emails about bills or seeing the old company’s logo online makes my chest tighten and I feel this wave of dread, like I’m right back in that office being told to pack my things. Even small reminders—someone mentioning layoffs on the news—can leave me on edge for the rest of the day.

What’s really bothering me are these strange experiences I’ve had, mostly at night but a couple of times during the day too. I’ll hear someone say my name, clear as day, or catch a glimpse of a shadow or figure out of the corner of my eye, and when I look properly there’s no one there. I can’t always tell if it’s just my mind playing tricks on me from the stress or something else, but it’s starting to worry me and my wife.
D019-D005_h001.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D005_h001.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D019-D005_h002.question:

I can’t focus on my work; I end up just staring at the cursor because I’m bracing for something bad to happen again.

What’s scaring me most is that sometimes I hear things that I’m not sure are really there—like a voice saying my name or a faint whisper when the apartment’s quiet. Once or twice I’ve seen something out of the corner of my eye, like a shadow moving, but when I look, nothing’s there. I keep wondering if it’s just stress or if I’m actually losing it.
D019-D005_h002.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia

    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D005_h003.question:

Sometimes when I’m alone and it’s quiet, I hear things I can’t quite explain—like someone calling my name from the hallway, or a faint radio playing in another room when there’s nothing on. Once or twice I’ve seen a shadow out of the corner of my eye that disappeared when I turned to look. I can’t always tell if it’s my nerves, my age, or something else, but it leaves me feeling unsettled and jumpy most of the day.

A. Acute Stress Disorder

    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
